To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miRNAs are important for regulating synaptic protein expression in neurons and that they are essential for synaptic plasticity.
“miRNA-mediated translational repression is essential for synaptic plasticity and memory formation.”
miRNAs regulate the expression of synaptic plasticity genes by controlling their translation and trafficking.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of post-translational gene regulation in synaptic plasticity and the mechanisms by which RNA-binding proteins, miRNA and other regulatory factors interact to regulate gene expression in the post-synaptic neuron.
how the brain uses post-transcriptional mechanisms to control neuronal function and how defects in this system can lead to neurological disease.
the mechanisms that regulate mRNA transport and translation in neurons, with the goal of understanding how these processes are altered in disease states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a long way to go before we understand the full extent and importance of post-transcription gene regulation in the brain.
the post-synaptic mRNA trafficking machinery, including miRNA, are essential components for synaptic plasticity.
the mechanisms that regulate mRNA transport, stability and translation are complex, dynamic and not fully understood, but are essential for normal neuronal function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the miRNA-mediated gene silencing pathway may be the missing component in the complex post-transcriptional control of neuronal gene regulation.
the miR-124 family is an important component of the neuronal post-transcriptional regulatory network that supports the activity dependent plasticity of the mammalian brain.
the miRNA-mediated post-transcriptional silencing pathway is a key player in the regulation of synaptic plasticity and memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the miR-124 family of miRNA may play a central role in regulating the expression of synaptic plasticity-related mRNAs and proteins.
miRNA may play an essential role in the regulation of post-transcriptionally controlled gene expression in neurons.
the miRNA machinery, and perhaps other RNA-binding proteins, are likely to be involved in regulating synaptic gene expression.
